_README: Scripts that are KNOWN to fail on master right now. runVerifySuite treats a
listed script's failure as EXPECTED and does not fail the run — which is what
makes a zero-red CI gate landable on a tree that has a deliberately-red harness.
THIS LIST IS NOT A MUTE BUTTON. A listed script that PASSES fails the suite,
loudly, as a STALE entry. That is the property that stops an allowlist rotting
into a rug: you cannot fix a bug and leave its harness suppressed, and you
cannot park a flaky script here and forget it. Removing the entry is part of
the fix, in the same commit.
Every entry needs a reason someone can act on. 'flaky' is not a reason.

verifyRunFinalizesOnSettle_KNOWN_OPEN.js.reason: RED BY DESIGN. This harness exists to stay red until the known-open run-finalization bug is fixed; the _KNOWN_OPEN suffix is the contract. It is the reason a zero-red gate could not previously be adopted at all.
verifyRunFinalizesOnSettle_KNOWN_OPEN.js.removeWhen: the run-finalization bug is fixed — delete the harness's _KNOWN_OPEN suffix and this entry together

verifyArchiveDigestRelease.js.reason: Pre-existing failure on master, unowned. Its E14 MONEY scan reports 'expected >= 8 Ad rendering->queued requeue writes, scan found 0 — the scan is broken', i.e. the harness's own scanner is not matching the current call shape rather than the guard being absent. Needs someone to repair the scan.
verifyArchiveDigestRelease.js.removeWhen: the E14 scan is repaired to match the current requeue call shape
